findings.title: `include_website_name` is missing the trailing `?` and is never invoked
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers decides whether to emit an attribute by calling `include_<attr>?` (with a question mark). The new method is defined as `include_website_name` (no `?`), so it is never called and the condition is ignored. As a result `website_name` is always serialized, emitting `website_name: null` for every user with no website (and any other case the guard was meant to exclude). It should be renamed `include_website_name?` to match the convention used by every other include check in this file (`include_email?`, `include_user_fields?`, etc.).

findings.title: `website_name` bypasses the untrusted-attribute restriction and leaks a TL0 user's website domain
findings.body: `website` is declared in `untrusted_attributes`, so its `include_website?` returns false when `scope.restrict_user_fields?(object)` is true (e.g. a TL0 user viewed by anonymous). The new `website_name` attribute is a plain attribute and its include condition only checks `website.present?`, not `restrict_user_fields?`. So even though `website` is suppressed, `website_name` is still emitted and discloses the user's website host/path to viewers who are explicitly not allowed to see that field. Add `website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (or gate its include condition on `scope.restrict_user_fields?`) and add a spec covering the TL0/anonymous case with a website set.
